retrieval.issue:
yq: {$a} inside object construction should silently produce zero output, matching real yq's COLLECT_OBJECT quirk

## Summary

Follow-up from #2724. That issue fixed jq mode's `{$a}` object-construction
shorthand (and the `{$a: expr}` dynamic-key form). yq mode was deliberately
left untouched there -- it still raises the same pre-existing parse error
it always has ("expected identifier, found '$'") -- because real yq's
actual behavior for this shape is a third, unrelated thing: not an error,
and not jq's `{"a":1}` either.

## What real yq actually does

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '1 as $a | {$a}'
$ echo $?
0
```

Empty stdout, exit 0. `--verbose` shows why: yq's `{...}` object-
construction grammar has **no shorthand concept at all** -- confirmed
separately that even the plain (non-`$`) field shorthand is rejected
outright at the lexer level:

```console
$ printf 'x: 1\n' | yq '{x}'
Error: 1:2: lexer: invalid input text "x}"
```

So `{$a}` isn't sugar in real yq -- it's `$a` (an ordinary `GET_VARIABLE`
op) evaluated as a bare, non-`key: value` entry inside `COLLECT_OBJECT`.
The verbose log shows `COLLECT_OBJECT` degrading on an odd/unpaired input:
`"collectObjectOperation, length of rotated is 0"` -> `"PROCESSING
VARIABLE DONE, got back: 0"` -> `"no matching results, nothing to
print"`. It's an incidental quirk of yq's object-collection operator
handling a non-pair entry, not a deliberate feature.

## Why this is separate from #2724

Reproducing this needs new **evaluator**-level behavior (an object-
construction entry that consumes zero pairs and yields nothing), not a
parser change -- #2724's fix was purely parse-time desugaring. It also
interacts with a pre-existing, already-shipped (and separately
undocumented) succinctly extension: succinctly's yq mode *already* accepts
the plain `{x}` shorthand as sugar for `{x: .x}`, which is itself a
divergence from real yq's lexer-level rejection shown above -- so there
are now two separate open questions about how far yq mode's object-
construction sugar should extend past real yq's much stricter grammar,
not one.

## Suggested next step

1. Decide the target: reproduce real yq's exact "bare non-pair entry
   degrades the whole construction to zero output" behavior (ADR-0018's
   preferred bug-for-bug default), or make a documented, deliberate call to
   keep succinctly's existing shorthand-sugar convenience extension and
   accept the divergence (recording it in
   `docs/compliance/yq/limitations.md`, which currently has no entry for
   object-construction shorthand of any kind despite the plain `{x}` case
   already existing and diverging).
2. Whichever is chosen, also close the parallel gap for the plain `{x}`
   shorthand noted above -- it's the same question, just discovered a level
   up.
